title: The Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954 and Rules 1955
authority: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare / Ministry of Ayush / Central Consumer Protection Authority

sections.heading: Prohibition of Advertisement of Certain Drugs for Treatment of Certain Diseases
sections.relevance: Strict legal restriction on advertising Ayurvedic formulations for scheduled conditions.

sections.heading: Prohibition of Advertising Cures for Schedule Diseases (Diabetes, Cancer, Obesity)
sections.text: No person shall take any part in the publication of any advertisement referring to any drug in terms which suggest or are calculated to lead to the use of that drug for the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment or prevention of any disease, disorder or condition specified in the Schedule (including Diabetes, Cancer, Obesity, Blood Pressure, and Infertility).
sections.relevance: Direct statutory ban and criminal offense for claiming 100% cure for Schedule conditions in newspaper, television, or online advertisements.

sections.heading: List of 54 Prohibited Diseases and Conditions for Advertisement
sections.text: Advertisements promising cure or mitigation are strictly prohibited for conditions including: Diabetes, Cancer, Blindness, Cataract, Deafness, Epilepsy, Female Diseases (infertility), Fits, Heart Diseases, High/Low Blood Pressure, Kidney Stones, Leprosy, Leucoderma, Paralysis, Rheumatism, Sexual Impotence, Stammering, Tuberculosis, Height increase, and Obesity.
sections.relevance: Absolute compliance barrier for digital marketing, e-commerce claims, and social media campaigns.

sections.heading: Prohibition of Misleading Advertisements Relating to Drugs
sections.text: No person shall take any part in the publication of any advertisement relating to a drug if the advertisement contains any matter which directly or indirectly gives a false impression regarding the true character of the drug, or makes a false claim for the drug, or is otherwise false or misleading in any material particular.
sections.relevance: Enforced actively by CCPA and State AYUSH licensing officers against deceptive influencer promotions.
